instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.

MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each); very short answers carry 2 marks (30–50 words); short answers 3 marks (50–80 words); long answers 5 marks (80–120 words).

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Find the number of moles: (a) in 36 g of water (b) in 11.2 L of N2 at STP.
questions.answer:
(a) Molar mass of H2O = 18 g, so 36/18 = 2 mol.
(b) 11.2/22.4 = 0.5 mol.

questions.q: (a) Write the equation for the preparation of iodobenzene from the diazonium salt. (b) Why is Cu not required here?
questions.answer: (a) C6H5N2+Cl− + KI → C6H5I + N2 + KCl. (b) Iodide is a good nucleophile and displaces N2 directly.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is an atomic mass unit (amu)?
questions.answer: It is exactly 1/12 of the mass of one carbon-12 atom, equal to 1.66 × 10^-27 kg. Atomic masses are expressed relative to it.

questions.q: What are isoelectronic species? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Species having the same number of electrons. Examples: Na+, Mg2+ and Ne (10 electrons each); also Cl− and Ar (18 electrons).

questions.q: What is meant by bond order? Calculate it for N2.
questions.answer: Bond order = ½(number of bonding electrons − number of antibonding electrons). N2 has 10 bonding and 4 antibonding electrons: (10 − 4)/2 = 3.

questions.q: What is meant by relative lowering of vapour pressure? Write the relation with mole fraction.
questions.answer: (p° − p)/p° is the relative lowering of vapour pressure; it equals the mole fraction of the non-volatile solute, x_B.

questions.q: What is entropy? Predict its sign for the evaporation of water.
questions.answer: Entropy is a measure of the randomness or disorder of a system. On evaporation, disorder increases, so ΔS is positive.

questions.q: Why is carboxylic acid more acidic than phenol?
questions.answer: The carboxylate ion is stabilised by resonance with the negative charge shared equally between two electronegative oxygens, whereas in the phenoxide ion the charge is spread onto less electronegative carbons.

questions.q: How can primary, secondary and tertiary amines be distinguished by Hinsberg's reagent?
questions.answer: Benzenesulphonyl chloride gives with 1° amine a sulphonamide soluble in alkali; with 2° amine an insoluble sulphonamide; and no reaction with 3° amines.

questions.q: What are hormones? How are they transported?
questions.answer: Chemical messengers secreted by endocrine glands directly into the blood; they are carried by the blood to the target organs where they produce specific effects.

questions.q: Differentiate between natural rubber and vulcanised rubber.
questions.answer: Natural rubber is soft, sticky and weak, with cis-polyisoprene chains; vulcanised rubber is heated with sulphur, which cross-links the chains, giving hardness, elasticity and resistance to heat and solvents.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: A compound contains 40% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen. Find its empirical formula. (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.answer:
Moles: C = 40/12 = 3.33; H = 6.7/1 = 6.7; O = 53.3/16 = 3.33.
Dividing by 3.33: C : H : O = 1 : 2 : 1.
Empirical formula = CH2O.

questions.q: Calculate the molar mass of K2SO4 if a solution of 2.5 g of it in 100 mL has an osmotic pressure of 10.6 atm at 300 K, assuming complete dissociation (R = 0.0821 L atm K^-1 mol^-1).
questions.answer:
With complete dissociation i = 3 and π = i (w/M)(RT/V).
M = i w R T / (π V) = 3 × 2.5 × 0.0821 × 300 / (10.6 × 0.1)
= 184.7 / 1.06 = 174 g mol^-1.

questions.q: Calculate the standard Gibbs energy change and equilibrium constant of Zn + Cu^2+ → Zn^2+ + Cu (E°cell = 1.10 V, n = 2, F = 96500 C mol^-1).
How is hydrogen chloride prepared in the laboratory? Why is it called a strong acid?
questions.answer: NaCl + H2SO4 (conc.) → NaHSO4 + HCl at 420 K (and at higher temperature Na2SO4). In water it ionises completely: HCl + H2O → H3O+ + Cl−, hence a strong acid.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) Define Gibbs energy. (b) Write the conditions of spontaneity. (c) For a reaction ΔH = −40 kJ and ΔS = −100 J K^-1 find the temperature below which it is spontaneous.
questions.answer:
(a) G = H − TS, the maximum useful (non-expansion) work obtainable from a process at constant T and p.
(b) ΔG < 0 spontaneous; ΔG = 0 equilibrium; ΔG > 0 non-spontaneous.
(c) ΔG = ΔH − TΔS = 0 at T = ΔH/ΔS = −40000/−100 = 400 K; below 400 K, ΔG is negative, so the reaction is spontaneous.

questions.q: (a) Explain why BaSO4 is insoluble but MgSO4 soluble. (b) State the uses of quicklime and slaked lime. (c) Write three biological roles of calcium and magnesium.
questions.answer:
(a) The hydration enthalpy of the small Mg^2+ exceeds the lattice enthalpy and the salt dissolves, whereas for the large Ba^2+ the lattice enthalpy exceeds hydration enthalpy.
(b) Quicklime: in making cement, glass and steel as flux, drying agent; slaked lime: whitewash, softening of water and mortar.
(c) Ca^2+ in bones and teeth, blood clotting, muscle contraction; Mg^2+ in chlorophyll and enzyme action.
